---
title: "Focus-follow: move the overlay to the focused monitor"
author: "Yun Jiang"
---

# Plan — overlay follows the focused monitor

## Objective

While the hint overlay is up (typically continuous mode), switching the foreground
window to another monitor (Alt+Tab / Win+Tab — both already pass through) currently
leaves the labels on the old monitor. The overlay should **move to the newly
focused monitor**, reusing that monitor's pre-built session — the same swap Tab
makes, but driven by a focus change instead of a keypress.

User note: some monitors are **portrait** — geometry must come from each monitor's
own pre-built session (already true: `BuildMonitorSessions` generates one grid per
monitor with per-aspect zone alignment), never from a shared landscape assumption.

## Approach

- **Edge-triggered follow.** `OverlayView` polls the foreground window's monitor
  (~200 ms `DispatcherTimer`, same simplicity-over-SetWinEventHook trade the
  quadrant guide makes). Only a *change* from the last seen monitor acts — Tab
  cycling (which does not change the foreground window) is never fought.
- **Session swap, no re-enumeration.** `OverlayViewModel.SwitchToMonitor(Rect)`
  finds the session whose `OwningWindowBounds` equals the new monitor's physical
  bounds and `LoadSession`s it: `Bounds` change repositions the window
  (`ApplyBounds`), labels regenerate for that monitor's count, prefix + pan reset —
  identical semantics to `CycleMonitor`.
- **Scope guard.** Only the multi-session Grid + Screen overlay follows
  (`CanFollowForegroundMonitor`). Zone mode is single-monitor by design; quadrant
  mode's four sessions share one monitor's bounds, so a bounds match could not
  pick the right quadrant; Automation / Grid+Window are single-session. Unknown
  monitor (plugged in after open) → no-op.

## Files

- `src/HuntAndPeck/ViewModels/OverlayViewModel.cs` — add `SwitchToMonitor(Rect)` +
  `CanFollowForegroundMonitor`.
- `src/HuntAndPeck/Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs` — foreground-monitor poll timer
  (start on load when capable, stop on close).
- `src/HuntAndPeck.Tests/ViewModels/OverlayViewModelTest.cs` — tests: switch by
  bounds (landscape ↔ portrait), prefix/pan reset, same/unknown monitor no-op,
  capability gates (single-session, quadrant).
- `CLAUDE.md` — document the behavior in the monitor-cycling bullet.

## Risks / verification

- Bounds equality relies on both sides coming from the WinForms `Screen` API in
  the same process (same virtualization) — the same pattern the guide's
  `ApplyFocusedMonitor` and `BuildMonitorSessions` already use.
- Cross-DPI moves use the load-time cached transform — unchanged from Tab cycling
  today (process is system-DPI aware; no manifest).
- Verify: CI compile + xUnit green; on-box: open overlay on monitor A, Alt+Tab to
  a window on the portrait monitor → labels move there within ~200 ms; Tab
  cycling still works and is not bounced back by the poll.
